entries.subject: A colour for Epsilon Indi Bb
entries.finding: The only resolved spectra of Epsilon Indi Bb, from King et al. (2010, A&A 510, A99; VizieR J/A+A/510/A99), are flux-calibrated but start at 630 nm. The missing 380 to 630 nm carries most of what the eye would see: with the gap filled by a ramp through the resolved V limit it holds 63% of the luminance, and the colour moves from sRGB (255, 0, 0) with the gap empty to about (255, 42, 0) with it filled, so a colour would be the fill, not a measurement. A blackbody at the temperature would misrepresent a brown dwarf's absorbed spectrum as well. It stays the shared neutral gray.
entries.revisitWhen: A flux-calibrated spectrum of the resolved component covering about 400 to 630 nm is published.
